notes: Every advertised OpenClaw gateway method is classified exactly once by its leading method group. 'implement' includes methods already present in Metiq and methods assigned to a future workstream; this file does not implement those methods.

groups.rationale: Core operator/runtime methods are part of the supported or planned Metiq control surface; gaps remain backlog rather than accepted incompatibilities.
Session lifecycle, collaboration, approvals, and protocol-v4 chat are the primary WS-A parity target.
Channel lifecycle, cron, approvals, and node/device management map to WS-A items A3 and A5-A8.
Memory diagnostics and migration controls align with the existing memory subsystem and WS-C lifecycle work.
Plugin approvals, package lifecycle, and skill curation belong to the WS-G platform/security roadmap.
Messaging and media methods extend existing channel, voice, and TTS capabilities rather than defining an incompatible product boundary.
Metiq implements durable profiles, preferences, and configured role metadata keyed by authenticated Nostr pubkey; email-primary account semantics remain an explicit identity adaptation.
These methods are OpenClaw-branded editor/setup or Control UI integrations; Metiq exposes its own Web UI and migration surfaces instead.

Terminal PTY sessions (including the attach/list/text/upload helpers), attach.* MCP-loopback grants, workspace-rooted fs.listDir, the git worktree lifecycle, the per-session board store (including the view-ticket surface and sandboxed frame host), gateway conversations, the durable question.* operator-question lifecycle, the ephemeral taskSuggestions.* registry, and the mcp.app.* MCP-App view surface are implemented as WS-native gateway surfaces in the A7 pass.

non_advertised_divergence_note: OpenClaw also defines product-specific methods that are hidden (advertise: false) or absent from the pinned descriptor catalog, so they never become triage-group entries above. swarmstr-u6gn.8 classified those long-tail families as intentional divergences; the authoritative per-method list lives in docs/parity/gateway-long-tail-2026-08.json and the family/rationale summary is mirrored here.

non_advertised_divergences.rationale: Metiq has no browser-push service, VAPID key lifecycle, or push subscription store; notifications flow through Nostr/channel events.
Metiq does not own GitHub OAuth, hosted project search, or a GitHub publication lifecycle; repositories and worktrees are operator-managed.
Metiq is a daemon and has no OpenClaw desktop worker host/process model.
There is no portal process/window lifecycle in Metiq.
Metiq exposes durable tasks and lifecycle gateway events instead of an OpenClaw progress-card projection.
These bind to OpenClaw's Control UI and GitHub preview model; Metiq has its own Web UI, board, artifact, and worktree surfaces.
Metiq authenticates with Nostr identities/device pairing and invokes its internal hook manager directly; it has no web-login or native-hook relay RPC.
WebSocket connection establishment is a transport handshake, not an RPC. chat.inject bypasses authenticated Nostr/session ingress and violates Metiq's event-driven routing contract.
Opening a host editor is a UI/OS side effect; Metiq already exposes config get/set/apply/patch/schema surfaces.

method_notes.chat.abort: Operator abort remains unconditional. Busy queue-mode interrupt is tool-aware: it aborts only when active tools are interruptible and otherwise defers newest input as urgent active-run steering.
method_notes.config.schema.lookup: Returns schema for a specific config path; full schema when path is empty.
